findings.claim: The catalog contradicts the README's new day split. module.json sourceCoverageNotes still say "S10 is a Concept day with no lab overlay". The lab reasons in the three S10 topic.json files still say "S10 is a Concept day with no lab overlay ... the validation-errors-and-testing module lab (S9) has learners finish and run MockMvc tests". But README line 11 places Tasks 4, 5, 7 and 8 on S10 "in the day's coding-lab blocks". The Standard Concept template has no block of that name; the closest are Short exercises 20 and Faded then fresh 40, assigned to platform coding practice (html-css-js intake, Concept row). So the placement is a pacing decision that no catalog or intake text records.

findings.recommendation: Update module.json and the three topic.json lab reasons to say the module lab spans S9 (Tasks 1, 2, 3, 6) and S10 (Tasks 4, 5, 7, 8). In the README, name the S10 Concept blocks the lab uses, and have the reconciler record the pacing decision.

findings.claim: Task 5 step 2 asks the learner to predict the problem body of a method-validation failure and says "The ProblemDetail page shows how Spring builds these bodies". No Spring page shows that body's title or detail; the ProblemDetail page shows only the request-body validation example. A learner following the page will predict that example's detail and be wrong. That can be a fair predict-then-observe step, but the README does not warn that this is a different case. The test also accepts any value once the learner copies the real one from the failure message, so the prediction stays self-checked; the README says so implicitly ("compare it with your prediction and work out why it differs").
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence to step 2: the page's example is a request-body validation failure, this one comes from method validation on a path variable, so predict what differs and why (the bean-validation page names the exception). Alternatively, predict the Task 1 body-validation case that the page does show.
